title: Follow-up Actions on Lapses at Public Agencies Reported in Auditor-General's Report
what_it_is: Follow-up Actions on Lapses at Public Agencies Reported in Auditor-General's Report

sections.label: Auditor-General report financial control questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Finance whether the FY2015/2016 Auditor-General's Report reveals systemic flaws, repeated breaches and whether officers will face action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Finance whether the lapses and inadequate financial controls reported by the Auditor-General in his Report for FY2015/2016 uncover any systemic flaws and how will the public sector entities strengthen their management of public resources to prevent future occurrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: asked	 the Minister for Finance whether the Report of the Auditor-General for FY2015/2016 has highlighted any repeated breach of financial regulations by any Ministry and, if so, whether any action will be taken against officers who fail to take remedial action to rectify the breaches.

sections.label: Unmodified audit opinion for Government
sections.summary: AGO has given an unmodified audit opinion for the Government Financial Statements this year, as in previous years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: AGO has given an unmodified audit opinion for the Government Financial Statements this year, just as in previous years.

sections.label: No systemic compliance weakness found
sections.summary: The report highlighted several lapses among agencies, but there is no evidence of systemic weakness in compliance within Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Page: 15 AGO's report highlighted several lapses amongst our agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: However, I can say with confidence from this year's AGO report and past years', that there is no evidence of systemic weakness within Government agencies with regard to compliance.

sections.label: Officers counselled or warned
sections.summary: Twenty-eight officers have been counselled or warned arising from this year's audit findings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Twenty-eight officers have been counselled or warned arising from this year's audit findings.

sections.label: Transparent accountable system tackling lapses
sections.summary: Lapses will continue to be tackled, and annual AGO reports reflect a transparent, accountable system where agencies submit to audit and rectify lapses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We will continue to tackle all lapses identified each year with the same resolve.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We have a system that is transparent and accountable, and with the Government responding to every weakness that is found.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The fact that we have found reports of lapses from AGO each year reflects this transparency and accountability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It is a part of the workings of a robust system – which includes a diligent and impartial AGO, and Government agencies that willingly submit to AGO's audit and have their lapses displayed openly and seek to rectify them promptly.

sections.label: KPMG found further AHTC control failures
sections.summary: The independent accountant KPMG found a further 70 control failures in AHTC, in addition to 115 found previously by AGO and statutory auditors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The independent accountant, KPMG found a further 70 control failures in AHTC in addition to the 115 found previously by AGO and statutory auditors.

sections.label: AHPETC payments to FMSS owners
sections.summary: AHPETC's payments to FMSS owners and directors were 22% of FMSS revenue in FY2012/2013 and 36% in FY2013/2014.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The total payments by AHPETC to FMSS owners and directors amounted to 22% of FMSS' revenue in FY2012/2013 and grew further to 36% in FY2013/2014.

sections.label: KPMG report on AHPETC controls
sections.summary: KPMG's July 2016 monthly report said progress remedying AHPETC's control failures has been slow, and AHPETC is working on remedial plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In its latest monthly report published in July 2016 – four years since AHPETC's auditors first voiced their reservations about the accounts – KPMG has stated that "progress remedying the control failures has been slow." We understand that AHPETC is working on its remedial plans.
